newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina Assembly approves $4.6 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina Assembly approves $4.6 bln budget.

text.p: South Carolina's General Assembly approved a $4.6 billion budget but abandoned plans to give major tax breaks to motorists and senior citizens.

Lawmakers approved the budget and then adjourned Thursday night. They had initially agreed to phase out the $651 million property tax on motor vehicles by 2006, trimming 12.5 percentage points off the tax each year.
They also agreed to eliminate state income taxes for residents over 65, raising the exemption to $11,500 from $10,000 this year, and eliminating the tax entirely in 1999.

But in negotiations this week, the proposals were withdrawn amid concerns they would squeeze the budget in future years. Only the increase in the exemption for those over 65 surivived, giving seniors a $62 million tax cut.
Instead, lawmakers said they would appoint a nine-member committee to study changes in the state's tax structure.
The budget still includes $227 million of property tax relief for homeowners, up from $213 million last year. It exempts the first $100,000 of assessed value.
The budget includes a $251 million general obligation bond bill to build prisons and fund construction and renovation at state colleges and universities.

Lawmakers also approved a bill capping local taxes at 3 percent for hotel rooms and 2 percent for restaurant meals and beverages. It authorizes counties to levy a one-cent local sales tax to fund infrastructure projects if voters approve.

The General Assembly also approved a proposal giving companies tax credits of up to 50 percent of their employees' income tax totals for five years if they invest at least $50 million in new facilities.

Left unresolved was a proposal to establish an infrastructure bank for road funding. Lawmakers will consider the proposal when they return on June 17 for a two-day session to consider any vetoes by Gov. David Beasley.

The infrastructure bank would issue $1.3 billion of road bonds for seven major construction projects, to be repaid with truck licensing fees and gasoline taxes. It would require annual appropriations of about $100 million.
